introduction_markdown: Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section 1 is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section 2 in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section 2 answer EITHER the a, b and c OR the d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark(s) for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.

figures.legende: Pulley system made of 3 wheels: effort of 2000 N applied to the free end of the rope, load of 8000 N hanging from the lower (movable) pulley.

incertitudes: Question 1(b)-(c) : la figure ne colle pas aux valeurs numériques. Sur le schéma, la poulie mobile est tenue par 3 brins de corde (brin gauche, brin droit, extrémité attachée au bloc), donc VR = 3 ; mais MA = 8000/2000 = 4 donnerait un rendement MA/VR de 133 %, impossible. Valeurs retenues : VR = 3 (lu sur la figure) et MA = 4 (calculé sur les forces imprimées) ; le corrigé signale l'incohérence au candidat. questions.corrige_markdown: A **machine** is a device that makes work easier to do: it enables a **small force (the effort) applied at one point to overcome a larger force (the load)** at another point, or it changes the direction or the point of application of a force (for example a pulley, a lever, an inclined plane).

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the value of the velocity ratio of the pulley system in figure 1? *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The velocity ratio is $\mathrm{VR} = \dfrac{\text{distance moved by the effort}}{\text{distance moved by the load}}$, which for a pulley system equals the **number of rope sections (strands) supporting the movable pulley and the load**.

In figure 1 the movable (lower) pulley is held by **3 strands**: the strand going up on its left side, the strand going up on its right side, and the end of the rope tied to its block. So **$\mathrm{VR} = 3$**.

*Note:* the force data of the question give $\mathrm{MA} = 4$ (see (c)), which is larger than 3. An efficiency $\dfrac{\mathrm{MA}}{\mathrm{VR}}\times100$ cannot exceed $100\,\%$, so the printed figures and forces are not fully consistent; the value above is the one read on the figure.

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the mechanical advantage (MA) of the pulley system. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The mechanical advantage is the ratio of the load to the effort:

$$\mathrm{MA} = \dfrac{\text{load}}{\text{effort}} = \dfrac{8000\,\mathrm{N}}{2000\,\mathrm{N}} = 4$$

**$\mathrm{MA} = 4$** (a ratio of two forces, so it has no unit): the machine lets a $2000\,\mathrm{N}$ effort balance a load four times as large.

questions.enonce_markdown: State two reasons why the efficiency of the machine is less than $100\,\%$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The efficiency of any real machine is less than $100\,\%$ because part of the work put in (the energy supplied by the effort) is wasted:

1. **Friction** in the pulley axles (bearings) and between the rope and the wheels: work is done against friction and appears as heat.
2. **The weight of the movable pulley (and of the rope)** has to be lifted together with the load, so part of the effort is used to lift them and not the load.
